audit.summary: I audited all 31 image assets in the game, the 10 site images and the in-progress scratch art. Each was measured at 960x540, 1280x720 and 1920x1080 using real Godot 4.7.2 renders (GL Compatibility on M1 Pro), an emulation of Godot's mipmap filtering, decoded S3TC and ETC2 plate textures, and alpha and colour metrics on the source files. The worst problems are in this order. (1) The new WOLF animation frames are too small: WOLF fills only about 9% of its 384x208 frame, so at its current height it is shown 1.3x enlarged at 960x540 and 2.6x at 1080p. (2) The approved v2 sentry wreck has a see-through band across its whole hull (rows 474-500, average alpha 181), which v1 did not have. (3) The active sentry blends into the background: 64% of its outline is within ΔE 10 of what is behind it, and only the red lens reads. (4) The title logo is drawn from a 512 px image at 88 px with mipmaps off, so its ring breaks into dashes. (5) WOLF, Rowan and the Director are 8-16x larger than their size on screen. That makes them soft and costs 8-10 MB of video memory each. They also have dark outlines and no top light, and blend into the background (edge contrast 1.01-1.18:1). Several props also have a near-black matte fringe, from 25% to 58% of their edge pixels. The props are 2-3x brighter and warmer than the room plates. The room plates are enlarged 1.35x at 1080p, and the title art 1.15x. Plate compression error measures 34.8-46 dB and is not visible at 3x. Nothing was played by hand and nothing was tested on a device. The repository is unchanged.
audit.findings_markdown:
## WOLF//OVERRIDE asset audit (2026-10-10)

Everything was measured, nothing guessed.

- **Real renders:** Godot 4.7.2 frames from a scratch copy of `apps/game`, captured with `--disable-vsync` (vsync on a background window was making frames crawl). Exact sizes were 960x540, 1280x720 and 1920x1080, using a SubViewport with a 960x540 2D override.
- **Sprite positions:** each sprite's opaque rectangle on screen comes from the engine's own transforms. It matches my calculated sizes: Rowan is 93.8 px tall (16x larger than shown), WOLF 82.9 px (10x larger).
- **Readability:** each sprite was rendered and then hidden on a paused frame, so its pixels can be separated from the background.
- **Filter emulation:** a Node script reproduces Godot's mipmap generation (2x2 averages) and GL trilinear or bilinear filtering. It compares the result with an ideal area-average downscale at 4 sub-pixel offsets, which gives the error, shimmer and sharpness figures.
- **Compression:** the S3TC and ETC2 `.ctex` files were decoded with Godot's own decompressor and compared with the source PNGs on premultiplied values.

"Density" below means source pixels per screen pixel. Under 1 means the image is enlarged and soft; well above 1 means wasted memory.

### 1. Density on screen (zoom 1.35 unless noted)

| asset | source | scale | 960x540 | 1280x720 | 1920x1080 | height at 960 | VRAM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rowan | 1024x1536 | 0.047 | **15.8** | 11.8 | 7.9 | 94 px | 8.4 MB |
| WOLF | 1902x1015 | 0.0733 | **10.1** | 7.6 | 5.1 | 83 px | 10.3 MB |
| Director (zoom 1.95) | 1024x1536 | 0.047 | 10.9 | 8.2 | 5.5 | 136 px | 8.4 MB |
| sentry active / down | 1024x768 | 0.07 | 10.6 | 7.9 | 5.3 | 59 px | 4.2 MB |
| relief vent | 768x256 | 0.097 | 7.6 | 5.7 | 3.8 | **22 px** | |
| arm panel / bolt panel | 512x512 | 0.14 / 0.15 | 5.3 / 4.9 | 4.0 / 3.7 | 2.7 / 2.5 | 87 / 79 px | |
| other props | 512x512, 512x768 | 0.2-0.302 | 2.5-3.7 | 1.8-2.8 | 1.2-1.9 | 104-194 px | |
| room plates (no mipmaps, compressed) | 1920x1080, 512x1080 | 0.5 | 1.48 | 1.11 | **0.74, enlarged** | | |
| title art (no mipmaps) | 1672x941 | 0.574, zoom 1 | 1.74 | 1.31 | **0.87, enlarged** | | |
| logo (512 raster, no mipmaps) | 512 | 88 px | **5.8, aliased** | 4.4 | 2.9 | | |
| [scratch] engineer animation | 256x384 | 0.37 | 2.0 | 1.5 | 1.0 | 94 px | 0.5 MB |
| [scratch] WOLF animation | 384x208 | 0.96-1.10 | **0.68-0.77, enlarged** | 0.5 | **0.34-0.39** | 83 px | |
| [scratch] doors A and B | 768x1280 | 0.107-0.118 | 6.3-7.0 | 4.7-5.2 | 3.1-3.5 | 178-190 px | 5.2 MB each |

Site images:
- The key-art hero uses `object-fit: cover` with the 1672 px source. Density is 0.57 on a 1440 px-wide 2x screen and 0.87 on a 1920 px 1x screen.
- The gameplay captures are 960x540 renders, taken at the lowest-detail game size. The landing page shows them at 960 CSS px, so density is 0.5 on 2x screens.
- WebP quality against the PNGs: key art 37.0-41.3 dB, captures 34.8-37.8 dB.

### 2. Filtering at game size (mipmapped sprites vs ideal downscale)
- **Logo:** the worst result, error 12.37 and shimmer 10.74 at 960. The real frame shows the ring broken into dashes and a stair-stepped outline.
- **Relief vent:** error 10.5, shimmer 7.6.
- **Tank:** error 9.7.
- **WOLF:** error 8.55, shimmer 5.1.
- **Sentry:** error 7.6-7.8.
- **Characters overall:** sharpness is 0.64-0.70 of ideal, so they look soft. This confirms the earlier audit's finding that mipmaps trade aliasing for blur at 10-16x density.
- **Plates:** error 0.4-1.2 at 960. Plates are smooth (noise σ 0.5-0.95), so skipping mipmaps is safe there. At 1080p they are enlarged.

### 3. Alpha quality
- **Sentry wreck (`junction-sentry-down.png`, committed approved v2):** a see-through band spans the full hull width.
  - It covers rows 474-500 (27 rows), with average alpha 181 and minimum 127.
  - 6.9% of the body is semi-transparent inside the silhouette.
  - v1 (`art/sentry/sentry-down.png`) has no band.
  - On a lighter floor at 1080p it shows as a light stripe above the treads.
- **Opacity is never exactly 255.** Every cut-out sprite and every mid and near plate has a body alpha of 252 or 253. Rowan's highest alpha is 254, so it has no fully opaque pixel at all. The background shows through about 1%. This points to an alpha-scaling step in the old pipeline. The new animation frames are at 255.
- **Black matte fringe on props:** semi-transparent edge pixels sit at 3-10% of the interior luminance at every alpha level, so this is a baked near-black edge, not premultiplied alpha. Share of edge pixels that are ≥15 L* darker than the interior next to them:

  | prop | share |
  |---|---|
  | corridor sealed door | 58% |
  | junction hatch | 57% |
  | arm panel | 41.5% |
  | relief vent | 41% |
  | coolant relay | 32% |
  | tank arm | 31% |
  | breaker | 30% |
  | safe point | 28% |
  | bolt panel | 27% |
  | valve | 25% |

- **Dark outlines on characters:** the inner 1-3 px are darker than the interior by 10-21 L* on Rowan, 16-20 on WOLF and 28-29 on the Director, on every side. The Director has no rim light at all.
- **[scratch] engineer animation:** the green key spill was turned cyan rather than removed. Edge colour shift is R -13, G +6 to +10, B +10 to +13, and 9-15% of edge pixels form a light halo. The cyan fringe is visible on the hair and jacket at 4x.
- **[scratch] doors A and B junction-sealed:** black fringe on 35-37% of edge pixels. B corridor-sealed is the cleanest, at 15%.
- **Not defects:**
  - The holes in the blown door, valve, bolt panel, mirror port and Rowan's arm gap are real negative space.
  - The tank-arm cable is drawn entirely in partial alpha (7.7% of that body is below alpha 250), so it fades out at game size.
  - Mid-plate partial alpha is on edges only (pipes and cables).
  - No stray pixel islands were found except 2 small ones (35 px) on the blown door.

### 4. Noise and over-detail
- Prop grain (Immerkær noise σ) is 4.0-5.5, against 0.5-0.95 for the plates and 2.2-2.5 for the characters.
- The share of detail too fine to show at 960 is highest on the sentry (46%), the relief vent and arm panel (35%) and Rowan (34%). That detail averages into mud, or shimmers when the sprite moves.
- [scratch] WOLF animation σ is 12.5-15.4 and the engineer animation 5.3-6.5, both grainier than the current sprites.
- [scratch] doors 1.7-2.4 and key art A 0.62 are clean; key art B is 0.83.

### 5. Compression (desktop S3TC, mobile ETC2, decoded through Godot)

| plate | S3TC format | S3TC PSNR | ETC2 PSNR |
|---|---|---|---|
| far | BC1 | 34.8-34.9 dB | 38.7-40.2 dB |
| mid | BC3 | 36.5-42.6 dB | 38.1-45.9 dB |
| near | BC3 | 36.2-40.3 dB | 37.7-43.0 dB |

- After the 960 display resample, error is 36.9-47.7 dB.
- The ratio of error across 4x4 block edges to error inside blocks is 0.94-1.27, so there is little block structure.
- The worst tiles show no visible blocking at 3x.
- Mid and near worst tiles first looked like 17-21 dB, but that came from RGB in fully transparent pixels, which `fix_alpha_border` fills before compression. On premultiplied values it is not a real error.
- ETC2 was decoded with Godot's decompressor but never rendered on a device.

### 6. Lighting and palette consistency
Lab values over opaque pixels:

| group | median L* | brightest 1% L* | b* (+ warm, − cool) | chroma C* |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| plates | 5-9 | 34-72 | -3.4 to -7.3 | 5.5-7.5 |
| props | 14.6-23.9 | 72-94 | -3 to +7.4 | 4.7-17.6 |

- **Brightness and colour:** props are 2-3x brighter in the mid-tones and lean warm or neutral, while the plates are cold blue. Most saturated: the exit hatch (C* 17.6) and the sealed door (14.5).
- **Black level:** every asset clips to L* 0 in its darkest 1%. The title's median L* is 1.3.
- **Light direction:** every prop is lit from the top. The top edge is +0.8 to +31 L* brighter and the bottom edge -8 to -21 darker, with a cool cyan-blue rim. The characters lack this top light (top edge -10 / -16 / -28 L*), so they read as unlit cut-outs next to top-lit props.
- **Design mismatch:** the current title art and the site copies draw WOLF as a furry wolf with armour plates, which does not match the plated robot sprite. Scratch key art A and B both fix this.

### 7. Readability in real 960x540 frames
"Lost" means the share of silhouette edge pixels within ΔE 10 of what is behind them. Edge contrast uses the WCAG luminance formula; the WCAG non-text guideline asks for 3:1.

| asset | worst shot | lost | edge contrast |
|---|---|---|---|
| coolant relay / breaker (dimmed, unpowered) | corridor start | 71.5% | 1.04-1.07:1 |
| Records purge queue | Records | 67% | 1.13:1 |
| Director | opening | 66.5% | 1.18:1 |
| tank arm | junction door | 66% | 1.11:1 |
| sentry | junction lane | 64% | 1.05:1 |
| WOLF | Records | 64% | 1.01:1 |
| Rowan | junction exit | 63% | 1.07:1 |
| best: blown door | junction lane | 39-40% | |

Every measured sprite falls far below 3:1.

### 8. Ranking, worst to best
1. **[scratch] WOLF animation frames.** WOLF fills about 9% of a 384x208 frame and is enlarged 2.6x at 1080p. Noise σ is 12.5-15.4.
2. **Sentry wreck (committed).** It has the see-through band, 6.9% of its body is semi-transparent, and 46% of its detail is too fine to show at game size.
3. **Active sentry.** 64% of its outline is lost against the background (contrast 1.05:1), it is only 59 px tall at density 10.6, and only the red lens reads.
4. **Logo.** It has no mipmaps and is shown 5.8x smaller than its 512 px image, giving the worst aliasing measured.
5. **WOLF sprite.** Density 10.1, error 8.55, 10.3 MB of video memory. Its grey-blue armour has C* 4.4 and blends into the background. Body alpha is 253 and it has a dark outline.
6. **Rowan.** Density 15.8 and soft (0.64 of ideal sharpness). No pixel is fully opaque, 5% of the body is at L* below 0.6, and the outline is dark all round.
7. **Director.** Its dark outline is the strongest of the characters (-29 L*), it has no rim light, and 66.5% of its outline is lost in the opening.
8. **Relief vent.** Only 22 px tall, error 10.5, black fringe 41%.
9. **Coolant relay and breaker.** 71.5% lost at the corridor start and black fringe 30-32%.
10. **Tank arm.**
11. **Records purge queue.**
12. **Arm panel.**
13. **Tank.**
14. **Junction hatch.**
15. **Corridor sealed door** (black fringe 58%).
16. **Site gameplay captures** (0.5 density on 2x screens).
17. **Bolt panel.**
18. **Safe point.**
19. **Valve.**
20. **[scratch] engineer animation.** The size is right, but the edges carry cyan key spill and a halo.
21. **Mirror port and exit hatch.**
22. **[scratch] doors A and B.** Clean, but about 2x larger than needed and 5.2 MB each; the junction-sealed versions have a black fringe.
23. **Blown door, sealed door and purge display.**
24. **Title key art.** Clean, but enlarged 1.15x at 1080p and drawn with the wrong WOLF design.
25. **[scratch] key art A and B.** A is cleaner; both are 1672x941, which is still too small for 1080p.
26. **Room plates.** Clean, compression is fine and they are very dark, but they are enlarged 1.35x at 1080p.

### What the redo should target (from these measurements)
- **Character size:** draw characters with their opaque height at about 2x the 1080p screen height:
  - engineer about 190-375 px tall (the new engineer frames are about right);
  - WOLF about 330-660 px wide;
  - sentry about 120-240 px tall.

  The WOLF animation needs a canvas at least 3x larger, or a tighter crop of WOLF.
- **Plates:** for full sharpness at 1080p, plates need 2.7 source px per room px, not 2. The expansion plan's "2 src px per room px" grid gives 0.74 density at 1080p.
- **Title art:** title art should be at least 1920x1080.
- **Logo:** set the logo's `svg/scale` to about 0.35-0.5 or turn on mipmaps.
- **Alpha:** re-cut alpha so bodies are fully opaque (255). Remove the black matte from prop edges and the cyan spill from the new frames, and remove the sentry-wreck band (or revert that part to v1).
- **Lighting:** add a top and rim light to the characters. Bring the props' grading toward the plates' cool palette, and lift the plates' mid-tones, or brighten the sprites' edges, to reach a usable silhouette contrast.

### Sources and caveats
- **Methods:**
  - The noise estimator is from Immerkær, "Fast Noise Variance Estimation", Computer Vision and Image Understanding 64(2), 1996.
  - The contrast reference is WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/#non-text-contrast).
  - Mipmap level choice follows the OpenGL 4.6 core spec, section 8.14.
  - I cited these from memory and did not fetch them this session.
- **Sprite parameters:** all scales, regions and zooms come from `scenes/main.tscn`, `records_room.gd`, `junction_room.gd`, `sentry.gd` and `room_depth.gd`. Import flags come from the `.import` files.
- **Limits of the evidence:**
  - All evidence is stills. Shimmer is the error at 4 sub-pixel offsets, not measured motion.
  - I did not compare the filter emulation pixel by pixel with real frames; only the sizes were checked against the engine.
  - Nothing was played by hand and nothing was run on a device.
- **Repository:** `git status` is clean. All Godot runs used the copy at `art-audit/game`.
- **Shared folder:** another process also wrote into `art-audit/` during this run: `dl/`, `dump_doc.py`, `grep_doc.py`, `evidence/band-contrast.json`, `measure.json`, `sources.json`, `openai-image-prompting.md` and `tf2-npar07.txt`. I left them untouched.

research.findings_markdown:
# Painterly 2D/2.5D art that stays clean at real display sizes: research and rules

All of this is **research plus source-texture measurement**. Nothing was rendered, played or tested on a device in this pass. Values come from the PNGs in `apps/game/assets`, so in-game light, glows and CanvasModulate will shift them.

**Search limit:** the session's web-search budget ran out after 2 queries. I fetched known primary URLs directly and did not use search-engine workarounds. For Hades, Darkest Dungeon, Gris, Blasphemous, Hyper Light Drifter, Little Nightmares and Unravel, only Wikipedia-level style facts were available, with no developer-talk content. The Ori: Will of the Wisps GDC talk was abstract only. The INSIDE slide PDF was too large to fetch.

## Measured state of the current assets
How sharp a plate looks depends on texels per screen px. Plates hold 2 texels per world px (1920 px drawn into 960 world px). Screen px per world px = (window height / 540) × zoom.

| Framing | Screen px per world px | Plate texel is drawn at | Mipmaps on plates |
|---|---|---|---|
| 960x540, zoom 1.35 | 1.35 | 0.675x (slight minification) | off |
| 1920x1080, zoom 1.35 | 2.7 | **1.35x magnified (soft)** | – |
| 2560x1440, zoom 1.35 | 3.6 | **1.8x magnified** | – |
| 1920x1080, opening zoom 1.8 | 3.6 | **1.8x magnified** | – |

**Value and detail per layer.** L* runs 0–100. "Detail" is the mean neighbour gradient in L* (higher means busier). Data: `evidence/measure.json`.

| Room | Far mean / median | Mid mean / median | Near mean / median | Detail far / mid / near |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| corridor | 10.6 / 6.2 | 6.5 / 4.2 | 4.6 / 2.1 | 3.6 / 4.2 / 2.4 |
| junction | 9.4 / 5.7 | **12.0 / 8.2** | 8.8 / 4.4 | 4.2 / **9.3** / 5.0 |
| records | 11.1 / 6.0 | 10.7 / 6.8 | 7.7 / 3.0 | 5.0 / **7.1** / 3.7 |

- **Junction is inverted:** the mid layer is brighter and busier than the far layer. Records' mid layer is busier than its far layer too.
- **Corridor runs in the right order** (far lightest, near darkest), but the medians are only about 2 L* apart.

**Characters against the walk band** (world y 300–440, mid composited over far). Data: `evidence/band-contrast.json`.
- Background median L* is 8.5 (corridor), 12.2 (junction) and 11.7 (records).
- Rim medians (the opaque pixels next to transparency) are L* 2.6 for Rowan, 0.8 for WOLF and 0.5 for the Director.
- Body medians are 19.8, 16.3 and 17.3.
- So the characters wear near-black outlines on near-black backgrounds. The body sits only about 5–11 L* above the band median.
- Props run brighter and busier than the plates: median L* 17–20, p95 58–72, detail 11–17.6. The sentry is the busiest at 17.6.

**Memory** (estimated from dimensions and import settings):
- **Totals:** about 74 MB as imported, or 118 MB if everything were plain RGBA8.
- **Characters:** 25.8 MB with mipmaps (WOLF 9.8, Rowan 8.0, Director 8.0).
- **Title art:** 6 MB.
- **The 9 plates:** `compress/mode=2`, meaning VRAM-compressed (S3TC on desktop, ETC2 on mobile with high_quality off), about 10.5 MB together.
- **Props:** lossless with mipmaps.

## Rules (each with its source and how it applies to WOLF//OVERRIDE)

1. **Size every texture to its largest on-screen size, not its master.** Ship about 2 texels per screen px at the closest supported framing. Paint masters larger and downscale offline (Lanczos), then turn on mipmaps.
   - Source: Dead Cells drops detail because its character is about 50 px tall ([Game Developer](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/production/art-design-deep-dive-using-a-3d-pipeline-for-2d-animation-in-i-dead-cells-i-)). Earlier audit: 6–18x minification causes the aliasing.
   - Here: Rowan peaks at about 250 px (2560x1440), so ship about 500 px of opaque height instead of 1478. That takes the three characters from about 26 MB to about 3 MB.
2. **Give the gameplay plate at least 1 texel per screen px at 1080p.** At zoom 1.35 that means 2.7 texels per world px (3.6 for the 1.8-zoom opening). A 960-wide room needs a 2592–3456 px plate. The 1440–1680 world-px rooms need 3888–6048 px.
   - Far layers can stay lower, because atmosphere hides the softness.
   - Once plates are oversampled, turn their mipmaps on, since a 960x540 window then minifies them.
   - Source: [Godot multiple resolutions](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/rendering/multiple_resolutions.html) says 1080p is most common and to enable mipmaps when downsampling.
3. **Use the right filter.** Non-pixel art drawn smaller than 1:1 should use LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS ([Godot CanvasItem](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_canvasitem.html)). Use mipmaps only where something is actually minified: they cost +33% and are wasted on textures drawn at a fixed size ([Android](https://developer.android.com/games/optimize/textures), [Godot import](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/assets_pipeline/importing_images.html)). Keep the per-sprite −0.5 LOD-bias shader from the earlier audit. The project-wide mipmap bias has no effect in this renderer.
4. **Use Lossless (or Lossy for big plates) for 2D, not VRAM Compressed.** Godot says VRAM compression "should be avoided for 2D". If memory forces it, use high_quality, which picks BPTC on desktop and ASTC on mobile ([Godot import](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/assets_pipeline/importing_images.html)). Android prefers ASTC with ETC2 as the fallback ([Android](https://developer.android.com/games/optimize/textures)).
   - All 9 plates are mode 2 today. Their L* 2–8 medians are exactly where block and banding artefacts show.
   - ETC2 has not been checked on a phone yet.
5. **Respect mobile limits.** OpenGL ES 3.0 only guarantees a 2048 px maximum texture size ([Khronos](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL-Refpages/es3.0/html/glGet.xhtml)).
   - Split plates into segments no larger than 2048 px (the level plan already segments them).
   - Crop alpha layers to their opaque bounds: corridor-mid is only 23.5% opaque, records-mid 27.9%.
   - Keep low and high variants per device class, and set a total texture budget for each room ([Android](https://developer.android.com/games/optimize/textures)).
6. **Design and check silhouettes first.** TF2 checked its characters as flat silhouettes with no interior detail ([Valve NPAR07](https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/apps/valve/2007/NPAR07_IllustrativeRenderingInTeamFortress2.pdf)). Ori began as black-and-white silhouette blockouts ([Xbox Wire](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/?p=4339)). Check every sprite as flat black at 94 px and 188 px tall.
7. **Make edges with value, not near-black outlines, in dark scenes.** TF2 emphasised silhouettes "with rim highlights rather than dark outlines" (NPAR07).
   - Ink styles (Darkest Dungeon's woodcut look, Hades' pen and ink, both Mignola-influenced: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darkest_Dungeon), [Jen Zee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jen_Zee)) only read when the ground behind the line is lighter.
   - Any line must survive minification: at 8x, a 2-screen-px edge needs about 16 px in the master.
   - Keep Fix Alpha Border on ([Godot import](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/assets_pipeline/importing_images.html)).
   - Here: the rims (L* 0.5–2.6) currently sit on an L* 8.5–12 ground.
8. **Give each depth layer its own value band.** With distance, contrast and saturation fall and colour shifts toward the fog colour ([Aerial perspective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerial_perspective)). TF2 kept distant scenery painterly and low in detail so it would not "generate high-frequency noise" (NPAR07).
   - Target: far layer lightest and lowest in contrast, mid layer carrying the playfield contrast, near foreground darkest and simplest.
   - Fix Junction and Records, where the mid layer is busier than the far layer.
9. **Keep detail low where the player looks.** "High frequency detail is omitted where possible", repetition stays minimal, and textures are "impressionistic … minimum level of visual noise" (NPAR07). Hollow Knight pairs clean, simple characters with intricate backgrounds ([Ari Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ari_Gibson)).
   - Check: walk-band plate detail should be at most about half the character's detail at display scale. Move racks and cables above head height or into the far layer.
10. **Make characters pop by value and a colour accent.** Inside is "mostly monochromatic", with colour "used sparingly to highlight … the player" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside_(video_game))). 11. **Use one lighting logic everywhere.** Keep one key-light direction, warm-to-cool shading, and shadows that go cool rather than black (NPAR07).
    - Paint plates neutral, and let CanvasModulate set the ambient light with additive sprites for glows ([Godot 2D lights](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/2d/2d_lights_and_shadows.html)).

    - Grade non-interactive props to the room. Ori gave each of its 7,000+ pieces its own lighting and colour ([Xbox Wire](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/?p=4339)). Let only interactive props stand out.
12. **Dither dark gradients.** INSIDE used dithering so subtle artwork is not "drowning in color-banding" ([GDC Vault](https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1023002/Low-Complexity-High-Fidelity-INSIDE)). That matters here, with plate medians around L* 2–8. Never VRAM-compress dithered dark plates.

One 2010 concept drawing guided Inside's whole look ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside_(video_game))). Ori avoided reused background pieces ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ori_and_the_Blind_Forest)).

14. **Run AI (Codex) generation as a controlled pipeline.** These steps come from the [OpenAI image-prompting guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-prompting):

Status: draft for Nathanial's approval. Nothing has been generated, imported, rendered in Godot or played. The repository was not touched.

Every number is labelled:
- **[measured]**: measured on 2026-10-10.
- **[proposed]**: a target. It must be re-checked against the approved style test.
- **[sourced]**: taken from a cited document.

Working files are in scratchpad/art-audit/bible/:
- qa_asset.py (automated QA)

- palette-card.png (colour reference)

## 1. Decisions
1. **Mood reference:** approved title art B (art/keyart/keyart-b.png). Cold blue-black, a wet mirror floor, overhead strip lamps and a cyan rim light. Red and amber appear only from practical lights.
2. **Clean means:**
   - readable silhouettes
   - no dark outlines
   - a top light and a cyan rim on every actor
   - bodies at alpha 255
   - 1-2 px anti-aliased edges with no matte or key spill

3. **Density (D, source px per world px):**
   - actors, props, doors and the sentry: 4
   - mid plates and near pieces: 8/3
   - far plates: 2
   - title: 1920x1080 in the game, from a 2560x1440 master
   - Screen px per world px = (window height / 540) x zoom.
4. **Generation:**
   - Codex built-in image_gen (edit mode) makes characters, props, doors, the sentry and far plates. The subject is always generated at least 1.25x the final size and downscaled, never upscaled.
   - Mid plates and the title need the imagegen CLI at 2560x1440, which needs approval and an API key.
5. **Transparency:** use native transparent output if the model supports it. Otherwise use a flat #FF00FF key, not green. Green spills against the cyan rim and the green safe light; today's engineer frames shift 6.3 at the edge [measured].
6. **Gate:** every file passes qa_asset.py A-H and gets a review sheet. No batch starts before the style test is approved.

C_top_light_dL: top-facing rim minus the core ≥ 0, target +10 (Rowan -12, engineer frames +11.2).
D_baseline: lowest row with ≥ 3 px at alpha ≥ 128 equals the spec ±1 px. For a directory of frames, same canvas and 0 px baseline spread on contact frames.
E_density: source px per screen px ≥ 1.0 at 1920x1080 at the asset's maximum zoom (far plates ≥ 0.7) and ≤ 4.5 at 960x540 gameplay.
F_cool_neutrals_b: median b* of low-chroma pixels (C* < 12) ≤ -1.
F_accent_dE_p90: p90 ΔE76 from saturated pixels (C* ≥ 25, L* ≥ 15) to the nearest bible accent swatch ≤ 18.
G_noise_display: Immerkær σ on luma at the 1080p display size. Actors and props fail above 6 (target 4.5), mid plate above 4, near above 3, far above 2.5.
G_hf_share: luma variance lost by a down/up resample to display size. Actors and props fail above 0.30 (target 0.20), mid above 0.25, near above 0.20, far above 0.15.
H_lost_share ≤ 0.35 and H_contrast_median ≥ 1.6, with ≥ 30% of the perimeter at ≥ 3:1. Pre-checked with qa_asset.py --bg; the pass criterion is Godot frames rendered with and without the sprite.
To write: walkline.py, the painted walkway edge within ±3 room px on flats and ±5 on ramps of the RoomProfile.
To write: seam.py, mean ΔE76 across each stitch ≤ 3 in the walk band, and L*/b* of the 96 px either side within 2.
To write: compression check (reuse tools/fringe_compress.js). Decode the .ctex with Godot's decompressor; premultiplied PSNR ≥ 38 dB per tile; block-edge to in-block error ratio ≤ 1.3.

To write: filter check (reuse tools/analyze.js). Mipmap and trilinear emulation against an ideal downscale at 960 and 1080p: error ≤ 6, shimmer ≤ 4. It also decides whether mid-plate mipmaps can stay off.
To write: anim_check. Hip-anchor drift ≤ 2% of height, loop-seam silhouette IoU ≥ 0.75 for walk and idle, left frames equal flip_h of the right.
To write: door_rmse. Silhouette RMSE between door families ≥ 0.25.
To write: provenance_check. Manifest entry per file, raw and final SHA-256, C2PA noted before stitching, prompts only in ignored notes.

Manual: design locks (WOLF 2 ears, 4 legs, 4 paws, robotic; engineer costume), silhouette naming at 94 and 188 px, the review sheet with Nathanial's approval, hands-on play before any feel claim, and an Android/iOS device check for ETC2/ASTC banding before any mobile claim.
bible.style_test_brief:
STYLE TEST: approve before any batch. One vignette of the Maintenance Corridor at target density, in two variants with identical layout. The winner becomes reference 4 for every later Codex call, and the QA thresholds are re-calibrated on it.

FRAME: exactly one 1080p gameplay view. 720 x 405 world px at 8/3 source px per world px gives 1920x1080. Side elevation, no vanishing point.

COMPOSITION:
- Floor: wet steel deck. The walk line is at row 800 (world y 440). Reflections only below it.
- Breaker station at x 15-27% (about 350 px tall). Dark steel, cool-graded. The amber status lamp (#e0936e) is the only warm light, with a small amber reflection on the floor.
- Engineer at x about 36%, about 186 px tall in the frame. Facing right, idle stance. Red jacket (#a01e29 / #5f0e17), cyan belt light, top light and cyan-white rim (#c3c5d7). No outline.
- WOLF at x 48-63%, about 307 px long. Standing, facing right, head turned back to the engineer as in key art B. Grey-blue plates (#656a72 / #292f37), cyan eye and seams (#4f8ab8). 2 ears, 4 paws.
- Coolant relay station at x 70-80% (about 320 px tall). Its cyan ring light (#30d0fc) is the accent.
- Lighting: two overhead strip lamps (#e3f6fe core, #385d85 shafts), one above the engineer and one above the relay. The darkest gap sits behind WOLF's back half, to test separation in the worst case.
- Far layer: pipes and a bulkhead in haze, lighter and flatter than the mid layer.
- Near layer: one dark rib at the left edge, ≤ 6% of the width.

DELIVERABLES PER VARIANT:
1. Plate without actors or stations: opaque 1920x1080. Generated at 1920x1088 on the CLI, or built-in 1672x941 upscaled 1.148x.
2. Four cut-outs on flat #FF00FF (or true transparency), matted per bible 5.4 at 4 source px per world px: engineer 280 px tall, WOLF 460 px long, breaker 388 px tall, relay 356 px tall.
3. A local composite (cut-outs scaled 2/3) at 1920x1080, 1280x720 and 960x540, plus 2x crops of the 960.
4. qa_asset.py JSON for every cut-out, and the H readability check for the engineer and WOLF on the composite.
5. One review sheet comparing both variants, with the current frame art-audit/frames/960/10-corridor-start.png as the before.

References: 1) the approved Rowan/WOLF sprites and the breaker/relay props (identity); 2) keyart-b.png (mood, light and palette only); 3) palette-card.png (colour only); 4) a crop of the approved corridor plates (rendering).

VARIANT 1, CURRENT LOOK CLEANED: the same painterly brushwork, texture and mood as key art B and the approved corridor plates, with every bible rule applied:
- no dark outlines
- top and rim light
- opaque bodies
- no detail under 2 screen px at 960
- props graded cool

Prompt add-on: "match the painterly brushwork of image 2, reduce fine texture and grain by half, keep large shapes".

VARIANT 2, GRAPHIC-PAINTERLY: the same palette, light and layout, with:
- 3-4 value steps per material
- large flat value planes, with soft painted transitions only inside light pools
- one panel line where there were three
- crisp shape-designed silhouettes and broad rim shapes
- a flat, light far layer and a pure-silhouette near layer

Prompt add-on: "shape-first graphic painting: flat value planes, minimal texture, crisp silhouettes, painterly only in light and atmosphere".

ACCEPTANCE BEFORE SHOWING NATHANIAL:
- every cut-out passes qa_asset.py A-G
- engineer and WOLF reach lost share ≤ 0.35 and median contrast ≥ 1.6 at 960x540
- design locks hold
- no text

Nathanial picks V1, V2 or a stated mix (for example V2 for actors and props, V1 for plates).
